entries.title: Marimar Martinez, others file police reports against Midway Blitz agents in new push for accountability
entries.summary: <p>Nearly a year after President Donald Trump launched his pummeling deportation campaign throughout the Chicago area, a group of residents began a new effort Monday to hold federal agents accountable for alleged crimes by filing police reports and demanding investigations.</p><p>They include<a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/immigration/2026/02/03/marimar-martinez-shot-border-patrol-chicago-speaks-out-after-good-pretti-deaths-i-am-their-voice" target="_blank" ><u> Marimar</u><b><u> </u></b><u>Martinez,</u></a> the woman<b> </b>shot<b> </b>five times by<b> </b>Border Patrol agent Charles<b> </b>Exum<b> </b>last October. Despite early hints of a federal<b> </b>investigation<b> </b>into the circumstances of her shooting, Martinez said she has yet to be interviewed by the feds<b> </b>in the 10 months since.</p><p>So for the first time Monday, Martinez called on state<b> </b>and local authorities to act, instead. She did so while joining eight others who marched into the Chicago Police Department’s Area 3 headquarters in North Center to report the feds’ alleged crimes.</p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/immigration/2026/05/21/special-prosecutor-midway-blitz-ice-trump-oneill-burke-cook-county" >Cook County judge rejects push to appoint special prosecutor to probe Chicago area deportation blitz</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p>“Today, I am demanding our local and state officials do their job and protect their citizens from these criminal conducts that [U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement] and Border Patrol have inflicted upon their victims,” Martinez said.</p><p>No federal agent has been charged with an on-duty crime connected to the Operation Midway Blitz deportation campaign despite widespread calls for accountability. Cook County Circuit Judge Erica<b> </b>Reddick<b> </b>in May <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/immigration/2026/05/21/special-prosecutor-midway-blitz-ice-trump-oneill-burke-cook-county" target="_blank" ><u>denied a request for a special prosecutor</u></a> who might have investigated the agents after asking whether anyone had actually filed a police report.</p><p>“Today, we are answering that concern,” said Berto Aguayo, an attorney and community organizer who alleges he and others were indiscriminately tear gassed by federal agents.</p><p>“When ordinary people have the courage to do their job as citizens, we expect that the people entrusted with enforcing our laws do their job,” Aguayo told reporters. “So today we have three words for the Cook County state’s attorney and any other investigatory body: Do your job.”</p><div class="Enhancement" class="Figure-content"><figcaption class="Figure-caption"><p>Attorney Brian Orozco speaks to reporters on Aug. 10, 2026, ahead of a “mass filing” of police reports alleging wrongdoing by federal agents during Operation Midway Blitz.</p></figcaption><span class="line"></span><div class="Figure-credit"><p>Anthony Vazquez/Sun-Times</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p>Cook County State’s Attorney Eileen<b> </b>O’Neill Burke’s office<b> </b>has stressed it is the responsibility of law enforcement agencies like the Chicago Police Department to investigate and build a case against agents accused of violating the law before her office can bring charges.</p><p>That makes Monday’s “mass filing” of police reports a possible key step toward that end, especially given the question posed by Reddick. A CPD spokesperson on Monday said each report “will be reviewed to determine whether there was a violation of local or state law.”</p><p>Meanwhile, Burke’s office formed a new task force in July to help guide and support such investigations — including by assessing whether criminal charges are warranted. Her office also <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/immigration/2026/02/19/chicago-ice-crime-border-patrol-trump-midway-blitz-alex-pretti-renee-good-eileen-oneill-burke" target="_blank" >released a charging<b> </b>protocol</a><b> </b>earlier in the year.</p><p>“No one is above the law — including federal agents — and the [Cook County State’s Attorney’s Office] will not hesitate to prosecute any case when it is supported by the evidence and the law,” Burke’s office said in a statement.</p><p>Cook County Commissioner Jessica Vásquez helped organize Monday’s filing effort. She said everyone reporting a crime had their own attorney and evidence to hand over to police. She also promised Monday’s event would not be the last.</p><p>Brian Orozco, an attorney assisting many clients Monday, said the alleged crimes ranged from illegal detention to battery to murder.</p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/city-hall/2026/07/21/chicago-police-directives-ice-agents-law-violations-operation-midway-blitz" >Chicago police set directives for collecting evidence on ICE agents suspected of breaking the law</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p>Jimmy Arce of the Illinois Accountability Commission also acknowledged “one very important voice who couldn’t speak with us because his life had been cut short.” It was a reference to Silverio Villegas González, a father who was fatally shot by ICE agents in Franklin Park last September.</p><p>The Illinois State Police <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2026/05/05/ice-midway-blitz-chicago-trump-silverio-villegas-gonzalez" target="_blank" >opened an investigation</a> into Villegas González's death<b> </b>in April.</p><p>Others have notably tried — and failed — to file reports with local police. <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2026/07/28/leo-feler-midway-blitz-trump-lake-view" target="_blank" ><u>Leo Feler</u></a>, a Lake View man who alleges agents illegally entered his home to chase after construction workers, said he was twice turned away from a Chicago police station.</p><p>The second time, he said an officer filed a report for criminal damage to property but he later received a call from a sergeant informing him they wouldn’t be moving forward with the case.</p><p>It wasn’t until <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/city-hall/2026/07/21/chicago-police-directives-ice-agents-law-violations-operation-midway-blitz" target="_blank" >just last month</a> that the Chicago Police Department finally issued formal guidelines on how to treat complaints against federal agents.</p><p>The guidance came after public outcry that CPD was not complying with a six-month-old mayoral executive order requiring the department to develop formal procedures for receiving complaints and collecting evidence against federal agents suspected of breaking the law.</p><p>The new guidelines require officers to notify their supervisors of a complaint and fill out an information report identifying the federal agent or agency involved, as well as witness and complainant information. Officers are required to give the complainant a report number.</p><p>Beyond that, complaints can be escalated upon review by supervisors. For instance, if the incident involved a death, shooting or other act of violence, a case would be referred to CPD’s detectives bureau and then, potentially, the Cook County State’s Attorney.</p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/public-safety/2026/02/06/how-can-chicagos-top-prosecutor-hold-ice-accountable" >How can Chicago’s top prosecutor hold ICE accountable?</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p>O’Neill Burke’s office<b> </b>in July formed a new task force to address the kind of investigations sought by Martinez and others Monday.</p><p>Known as the Federal Enforcement Action Felony Review Group, it’s meant to assist with “matters involving on-duty federal law enforcement activity, including immigration enforcement actions, conduct related to voter rights and election activity, and any other misconduct perpetrated by federal law enforcement that is potentially criminal in nature,” according to Burke’s office.</p><p>It’s expected to draw members from Burke’s felony review and grand jury units, among others, with preferences for staff with federal court experience.</p><p>While O’Neill Burke's office must approve any felony charges, local law enforcement have the power to make misdemeanor charging decisions on their own.</p><p>Martinez’s trip inside the Area 3 headquarters lasted about two hours. She later said it took officers at least a half hour to take down her statement. Once outside, she said she felt good about the whole experience.</p><p>“At 10 months, I’ve been waiting for this,” Martinez said. “I’ve actually been waiting for this to come out and speak up. It’s time. Change starts with us.”</p>

entries.title: Sky coach Tyler Marsh addresses DiJonai Carrington ejection, social media post
entries.summary: <p>SEATTLE — <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/chicago-sky" target="_blank" >Sky</a> coach Tyler Marsh said the focus coming out of the Fever game — which included DiJonai Carrington’s flagrant foul 2 on Sophie Cunningham and subsequent <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/chicago-sky/2026/08/09/dijonai-carringtons-white-privilege-post-awaits-response" >“WHITE PRIVILEGE” social media </a>post tagging the Fever — remains on basketball.</p><p>“I’ve spoken to DiJonai, obviously,” Marsh said. “She knows where I and we are … for her individually and for our team.”</p><p>When asked whether he thought the flagrant 2 designation was unfair, Marsh returned to the calls for <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/chicago-sky/2026/08/03/after-mercury-loss-sky-coach-tyler-marsh-rips-officiating-of-kamilla-cardoso-its-a-joke" >consistency in officiating</a> he has made throughout the season.</p><p>“I think that when we talk about consistency and officiating, it’s all parts,” he said. “I think there are other fouls that may have been similar that didn’t result in a flagrant 2. If one does, then all of them should.”</p><p>After the game, officials said the criteria for a flagrant 2 was met “since the contact was deemed unnecessary and excessive to a player in a vulnerable position.” They cited the “windup, impact, follow-through and high potential for injury" at the time of the foul. </p><p>Marsh acknowledged that losing Carrington to the ejection took the wind out of the Sky’s sails in what became a four-point loss, but reiterated that he did not believe the foul was intentional.</p><p>“I think the intent was to make an attempt on the ball,” Marsh said. “That’s how she plays. That’s who she is. She’s passionate. She’s hard-nosed. It’s unfortunate that’s what happened, but I don’t think that was what her intent was.</p><p>“She wanted to be out there for our team. At the end of the day, there's a lot that has come out of it. There’s a lot of vitriol at DiJonai’s expense. There’s a lot that she has to deal with as well. When we talk about protecting players, it should be every player.”</p><p>Marsh did not say whether he was disappointed that Carrington posted on social media after her ejection, instead acknowledging the power of social media and how quickly people can run with narratives that suit them.</p><p>“I don’t think it calls for a matter of policing our players,” Marsh said. “But I think everyone is aware of what can arise from that. I think DiJonai knows how we feel.”</p><p>Marsh has been critical of officiating throughout the season, particularly what he views as a lack of consistency and accountability. Asked whether racism and unconscious bias need to be addressed in officiating, he said that was for the league to determine.</p><p>“I think it would be ignorant to think that it doesn’t play a part in the grand scheme of society,” Marsh said. “But I don’t think it influences calls that happen with officiating.”</p><p>The WNBA did not respond to a request for comment.</p><bsp-list-loadmore entries.title: Bears sign veteran WR Ray-Ray McCloud, waive WR Kyron Hudson
entries.summary: <p>As injuries stack up at wide receiver, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >the Bears</a> signed veteran Ray-Ray McCloud on Monday. He will have a narrow path to make the final roster, but few of his competitors are as accomplished as him.</p><p>McCloud, 29, has played eight seasons and is not far removed from being a starter. He played every game for the Falcons, including 13 starts, in 2024 and had 62 catches for 686 yards and a touchdown, plus 10 rushes for 79 yards.</p><p>He has bounced around since, though. He began last season with the Falcons, then was cut in October. He resurfaced with the Giants soon after, but played just two games and hadn’t been in any organization until Monday.</p><p>He also has significant experience as a punt and kick returner, which could help him stick around.</p><p>The Bears <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/08/10/bears-luther-burden-groin-injury-preseason-miss-nfl-wide-receiver-practice-tyrique-stevenson" >will be without wide receiver Luther Burden</a> the rest of the preseason because of a groin injury and waived injured receiver Kyron Hudson on Monday to open a spot for McCloud.</p><p>McCloud was a sixth-round pick by the Bills in 2018 and gained some traction a few years later with the Steelers. He has played in eight playoff games, including Super Bowl LVIII with the 49ers. The Bears are his seventh team.</p><bsp-list-loadmore class="PageListH" data-module data-hide-authors="true" data-hide-categories="true" data-hide-dates="true" data-show-loadmore="true" ><a entries.title: Review: Kehlani delivers a joyful performance that’s both a party and a safe space to heal
entries.summary: <p>Sunday’s thunderstorms set the mood for listening to Kehlani’s self-titled fifth album — in the comfort of your own home. But the foreboding storms let up just in time for Kehlani to take the stage in front of 100,000 attendees at Huntington Bank Pavilion in what would be a jubilant night for the ascending R&B singer.</p><p>“To be able to be here tonight and you guys sold out every ticket available, I appreciate you. To be here when it was raining cats and dogs and boots and bagels and s--- outside, y’all are so real and I love you and I appreciate you,” Kehlani told fans during the sold-out Chicago stop of the Kehlani World Tour. And the turnout was a huge difference from her previous Chicago performances. “The last time I did Chicago [at Aragon Ballroom in 2024, it] was about 5,000,” she told the crowd.</p><p>It’s been a breakout year for the singer. Her latest album, featuring the hit “Folded,” hit No. 4 on the Billboard 200, becoming the biggest debut for an R&B album by a woman this year.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div out with friends at a fictional, queer and women-friendly nightclub, The Phoenix. The concept was also an allegory of coming back to life after enduring severe hardships and pain. It was emblematic of what her audience, people of color and queer people, have faced during the second term of President Trump, including the rollback of federal protections for LGBTQ+ people and the administration’s immigration enforcement campaign.</p><p>The show also highlights Kehlani’s own story of how her self-titled fifth album became one of the biggest turning points of her career with “Folded.” It led to her very first Grammy Awards for “Best R&B Performance” and “Best R&B Song” after years of being nominated. This was significant because she was one of the few musicians who spoke against the Immigration and Customs Enforcement arrests across the country while still achieving commercial success in spite of dealing with backlash.</p><p>The show’s six parts — “Morning,” “Home/Walk,” “Club,” “Afters,” “Walk Home” and “Home” — were a step-by-step musical journey. “Morning” saw Kehlani being brought out in bed, waking up with her dancers to “Anotha Lova.”</p><p>Throughout the evening, the show paid homage to Kehlani’s musical influences from the ’90s and early 2000s through dance routines and song sampling. Throughout “Home/Walk” and the DJ Waseel-led “Club” acts, the dancers performed hip-hop choreography reminiscent of an early 2000s R&B video. Each of them danced over songs like Ciara’s “Goodies” and Aaliyah’s “Rock The Boat,” with Kehlani dancing during the latter half.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Figure-content"><figcaption class="Figure-caption"><p>Durand Bernarr opens up for Kehlani Sunday at the Huntington Bank Pavilion at Northerly Island as part of the Kehlani World Tour.</p></figcaption><span class="line"></span><div class="Figure-credit"><p>Sterling Hightower/For the Sun-Times</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p>Kehlani’s powers shone the brightest in the closing acts, “Afters,” “Walk Home” and “Home.” Hopping back on stage in an all-purple outfit, Kehlani brought the audience back to reality after a night of pure fun. “I Need You” masterfully captured the emotional spirit of ’90s R&B that brings you deep into your feels. And the choreography on “Late Nights” carried that same pinpointed precision, as in Janet Jackson’s “Rhythm Nation” era music videos. It’s a case study of how an artist can take inspiration from their heroes without being a knockoff version.</p><p>“You guys played such a large role in the last year of my life; it turned a complete 180 on me. And I have to say thank you, and I have to take a moment — can we all say thank you, God, that we all have someplace tonight that is safe that we can gather and that we can celebrate joy,” proclaimed Kehlani.</p><p><b></b> New Jersey’s own The Arti$t is one of the crown jewels of Chicago-based Laka Films' No More Heroes imprint. The R&B singer represents a pivot for the label, beyond drill music. The Arti$t’s third project, “DND,” was released in April. Standing in the middle of the stage, the singer charmed the audience with her lovely vocals on songs like “S.I.M.P.L.E.” Her stage presence was so captivating that one fan yelled, “Sing to me, daddy!”</p><p>Riding high from his recent Grammy victory for “Best Progressive R&B Album,” Durand Bernarr was clearly in high form. Dressed to the nines in a sleeveless beige suit and multicolored scarf around his head and neck, Bernarr performed songs like “My Life” and “SHARP!” with bold, spiritual flair that’s reminiscent of a young Prince. His set had fans on their feet as if we were in the Black Church. It was Sunday after all. <b></b></p><p>Kehlani brought all three openers out to perform “Unlearn.”</p><p>“We were rushed on stage an hour early, but just know that these are the most talented people in the world. And it’s actually hard to go last and try to sing when these singing ass muh’f------ done hooted and hollered all over the stage before I got there,” Kehlani said.</p><p>“Unlearn” is her confessional closer that finds Kehlani being painfully honest about unlearning toxic behaviors from growing up in survival mode. And hearing all four voices combined felt as emotionally compelling as watching ’90s Disney films like “Aladdin” and “The Lion King” that were predominantly soundtracked by legendary R&B singers from the era.</p><p>Kehlani has long been a voice against injustice and creating space for the most marginalized. On Sunday, she gave fans the space to party, not to distract us, but to heal us all.</p><h3><b></b></h3><p></p><h3>Kehlani set list for Aug. 9, 2026, show at Huntington Bank Pavilion at Northerly Island</h3><p><b>I. Home</b><br>Everything<br>Cruise Control<br>Unlearn <br>Folded</p>

entries.title: Trump signs executive order calling for spacing out childhood shots
entries.summary: <p>NEW YORK (AP) — President Donald Trump on Monday signed an executive order calling for revamped <a class="Link" href="https://apnews.com/article/childhood-vaccine-schedule-trump-rfk-hhs-d04ba53d6820cc7194a4885e2418d132" target="_blank" >childhood vaccine recommendations</a> that promote his long-held belief that childhood shots should be spaced out into separate medical visits.</p><p>The order recommends separating the measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) vaccine into three different shots administered in separate visits, and directs the nation’s health department to improve vaccine research, says a White House fact sheet, first reported by The Daily Caller. Separate measles, mumps and rubella vaccines for children are not currently available in the United States.</p><p>Speaking about the order at the Oval Office on Monday, Trump also said that one-year-olds should have their shots separated out into five separate visits, though it wasn’t clear whether he was talking about all the vaccines they receive or specific ones.</p><p>Public health experts have raised concerns that spacing out shots as Trump suggests can lead to an increased risk that children become infected with a vaccine-preventable disease before returning for another visit. Childhood vaccines — and how and when to give them in combination — go through rigorous studies, and safety tracking continues for years as the shots are used.</p><p>Even as the order calls for revised vaccine recommendations, states, not the federal government, have the authority to require vaccinations for schoolchildren. The order will advise states with school vaccine mandates to consider updating their laws to reflect the administration’s recommendations, the fact sheet said.</p><p>Illinois still requires the traditional series of childhood vaccines.</p><p>Last December, Trump ordered HHS to review how peer nations approach vaccine recommendations and consider revising U.S. guidance accordingly. The department responded by cutting the number of <a class="Link" href="https://apnews.com/article/rfk-jr-vaccine-trump-science-autism-9b99621b01f11b7f0bdc81e5a0b82d2b" target="_blank" >vaccines</a> it recommends for every child, a move that has since been blocked in court.</p><p>In the months leading up to Monday’s announcement, Trump’s administration had largely pivoted away from talking about vaccine policy in favor of less polarizing topics like healthy eating and efforts to lower drug prices ahead of November’s elections. Polls show most Americans <a class="Link" href="https://apnews.com/article/vaccines-childhood-vaccinations-vaccine-mandate-kennedy-521201a8e4100f3cc1a8f1f5a7423b77" target="_blank" >still support school vaccine requirements</a>, though Republicans are less likely than Democrats to see them as important.</p><p>Still, Trump has been fixated on connecting autism to vaccines. He has recently ramped up pressure on Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. to identify the cause of autism, something Kennedy had pledged to do with new research unveiled last year. Trump publicly prodded the health secretary for an update on autism research in a Cabinet meeting last month.</p><p>“How are you doing on the autism research?” Trump asked.</p><p>“We will have an answer for you,” Kennedy said.</p><p>Scientific consensus and decades of studies have firmly concluded there is no link between childhood vaccines and autism. On Monday, Kennedy repeated his assertion that he believes an unknown environmental factor is to blame for rising autism diagnoses and said that his department will deliver research findings “as soon as they are ready.”</p><p>Monday’s order comes as school years are starting around the country and the nation contends with a measles outbreak that experts say could result in the U.S. losing its <a class="Link" href="https://apnews.com/article/us-measles-elimination-mexico-6f0bc8f7ef31d5ef82492e42ccb38e47" target="_blank" >measles elimination status</a>.</p>

entries.title: Adolescente fallecido en choque de scooter es recordado como alguien que ‘siempre estaba ahí para todos’
entries.summary: <p>Alex Blacio era "la roca" para todos.</p><p>Fue una presencia constante en su familia, según sus parientes. El adolescente jugó voleibol en la escuela intermedia y la secundaria —llegó a ser capitán del equipo varonil de Lake View High School el año pasado, donde estaba dispuesto a jugar donde fuera necesario— y a menudo se reunía con sus amigos de la secundaria para jugar en los gimnasios abiertos.</p><p>El lunes de la semana pasada, el joven de 16 años circulaba hacia el norte en la cuadra 4100 al norte de Western Avenue alrededor de las 3:35 p.m., cuando perdió el control y fue atropellado por un camión tractor, dijo la Policía de Chicago en un comunicado. Lo trasladaron al Illinois Masonic Hospital, donde fue declarado muerto, informó la policía.</p><div class="RichTextSidebarModule Enhancement" data-module data-align-center><a class="AnchorLink" id="module-1c0000" name="module-1c0000"></a> <div class="RichTextModule-items RichTextBody"><h3>La Voz Chicago WhatsApp</h3>Encuentra más noticias en nuestro canal de WhatsApp. <a class="Link" href="https://www.whatsapp.com/channel/0029Vb0XT1XCHDylm3rCs40P" target="_blank" ><b>Síguenos.</b></a></div> </div><p>Era su tercer día en su primer trabajo y, aunque no le tocaba turno, tenía ganas de tomar otro para ayudar a su familia, según contó su hermana mayor, Andrea Blacio.</p><p>"Mostraba tanto amor; siempre estaba ahí para todos", dijo. class="line"></span><div class="Figure-credit"><p>GoFundMe</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p>Los choques relacionados con scooters eléctricos han aumentado junto con el incremento de usuarios en los últimos años, lo que ha motivado una campaña de <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/transportation/2026/05/04/chicago-launches-e-scooter-safety-campaign-in-wake-of-recent-scooter-deaths" target="_blank" >seguridad</a> por parte de la Ciudad. El Departamento de Bomberos de Chicago respondió a casi 200 incidentes relacionados con scooters eléctricos en 2022. Ese número se había <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/public-safety/2026/06/05/scooter-escooters-lane-tech-safety-teenagers-crashes" target="_blank" >triplicado para 2025</a>.</p><p>Horas antes de la vigilia, un menor también resultó gravemente herido tras ser atropellado por un camión mientras circulaba en una bicicleta eléctrica en los suburbios de Crystal Lake, lo que requirió su traslado en helicóptero debido a "lesiones que ponen en peligro la vida", según funcionarios de Crystal Lake.</p><p>Aun así, los scooters eléctricos se han vuelto cada vez más populares entre los estudiantes de la secundaria Lane Tech College Prep, a menos de una milla al sur del lugar donde ocurrió el choque de Alex.</p><p>Hasta ahora este año, otros dos adolescentes han sido atropellados mortalmente por conductores mientras usaban scooters eléctricos en la ciudad: la joven de 17 años <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/news/2026/05/01/loved-ones-launch-fundraiser-for-venezuelan-teenager-killed-in-south-side-scooter-crash" target="_blank" >Astrid Alexandra Carrillo Noguera</a> y la de 15 años <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/crime/2026/03/22/girl-15-killed-while-riding-scooter-in-south-shore-hit-and-run" target="_blank" >Violet Harris</a>, quienes murieron en accidentes en el lado sur con casi un mes de diferencia esta primavera.</p><p>Seis personas en scooters o bicicletas fueron <a class="Link" href="https://api.chicago.gov/filenet5/servlets/getDocumentContent?applicationId=CompleteStreets&documentId=%7B601CB99F-0000-C917-A80A-59C827820B0F%7D" target="_blank" >atropelladas por automóviles y fallecieron</a> entre enero y junio, en comparación con una en el mismo período del año pasado. El número de muertes por tráfico —que la Ciudad había prometido eliminar para este año— se mantiene, en gran medida, donde estaba hace 10 años, tras un breve aumento durante la pandemia.</p><p><i>Traducido con una herramienta de inteligencia artificial (IA) y editado por los seres humanos de </i><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/la-voz" target="_blank" ><i>La Voz Chicago</i></a><br></p>

entries.title: Bears training camp report No. 11: Ben Johnson downplays concerns about injuries to DE Montez Sweat, others
entries.summary: <p>Breaking down <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >the Bears</a>’ Monday training camp practice:</p><h3><b>What happened</b></h3><h3></h3><p>The Bears held a walk-through at Stevenson High School in Lincolnshire, a quick drive from Halas Hall, and it was short and light of an NFL practice as could be. They went about 50 minutes, didn’t wear helmets or pads and went at a trot pace as Caleb Williams steered the offense through plays with a backwards cap, but didn’t actually pass. The only real throwing that took place was cornerback Jaylon Johnson playing catch with fans in the bleachers.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="en" dir="ltr">The rookies getting the crowd HYPED 😆 <a href="https://t.co/LUHma268IP">pic.twitter.com/LUHma268IP</a></p>— Chicago Bears (@ChicagoBears) <a href="https://x.com/ChicagoBears/status/2086892480344064160?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">August 10, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p></p><h3><b>Injury watch</b></h3><h3></h3><p>Injured defensive end Montez Sweat, left tackle Braxton Jones, cornerback Tyrique Stevenson and wide receiver Zavion Thomas didn’t participate, but coach Ben Johnson told the Sun-Times on Monday that none of those are long-term concerns. He also said wide receiver <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/08/10/bears-luther-burden-groin-injury-preseason-miss-nfl-wide-receiver-practice-tyrique-stevenson" >Luther Burden</a> will miss the rest of the preseason with a groin injury.</p><p>Those players and other injured Bears, including nickel cornerback Kyler Gordon and left tackle Ozzy Trapilo, signed autographs during practice.</p><h3><b>What’s next?</b></h3><h3></h3><p>This is going to be good. With an off day coming up Wednesday, the Bears will hold a scrimmage at Halas Hall on Tuesday afternoon that is closed to the public. It’s expected to be their most strenuous and competitive practice yet.</p><h3><b>Decisions ahead</b></h3><h3></h3><p>As the Bears approach their preseason opener Saturday against the Browns at Soldier Field, Johnson must decide if he’ll play his starters or let the Tuesday scrimmage suffice as their game-like work for the week.</p><p></p><bsp-list-loadmore class="PageListH" data-module entries.title: Chicago man gets 'time served’ in gun turn-in case that angered former U.S. Education Secretary Arne Duncan
entries.summary: <p>Nakia Smith says he walked into a Far South Side police station to get a gun off the streets.</p><p>Instead, he wound up behind bars.</p><p>Prosecutors say Smith, a convicted felon, was carrying a concealed firearm he was legally barred from possessing.</p><p>On Monday, Smith, 51, pleaded guilty to felony gun charges in a deal that spared him the possibility of serving at least six years in an Illinois prison. He was sentenced to time served for the time he spent locked up after his March 2023 arrest.</p><p>Smith spent seven months in the Cook County Jail before he was released in January 2024 on home confinement and electronic monitoring as the case moved through court.</p><p>After Monday’s hearing in Bridgeview, he was briefly returned to jail for processing before being released.</p><p>At his sentencing, Smith urged the Chicago Police Department to create a way for convicted felons to surrender firearms without risking prosecution for illegally possessing them.</p><div class="Enhancement" That’s what we’re trying to do. So it’s all the wrong messaging.”</p><p>The Chicago Sun-Times <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/the-watchdogs/2026/08/04/arne-duncan-education-secretary-gun-violence-cred-chicago-police-cpd" target="_blank" ><u>reported on Smith’s arrest last week</u></a>.</p><p>Smith’s legal odyssey began March 4, 2023, when he entered the Calumet District police station at 727 E. 111th St.</p><p>Smith says he asked to speak with a supervisor so he could hand over his coat, which held a .45-caliber handgun he says one of his workers had taken during a home cleanup job.</p><p>But Smith never got the chance to turn over the coat.</p><p>An officer at the front desk asked whether he was carrying a gun. When Smith said he was, officers took him into custody, and he was charged with illegal firearm possession.</p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/the-watchdogs/2026/08/04/arne-duncan-education-secretary-gun-violence-cred-chicago-police-cpd" target="_blank" >Gun case against Chicago anti-violence volunteer a ‘travesty,’ former Education Secretary Arne Duncan says</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p></p>

entries.title: MLB sets postseason schedule, which could include Cubs, White Sox
entries.summary: <p>At the pace the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs" target="_blank" >Cubs</a> and <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox" target="_blank" >White Sox</a> are going, both teams could make the postseason in the same full season for the first time since 2008. On Monday, MLB released when those games would be played.</p><p>The American League and National League wild-card series are scheduled for Sept. 29-Oct. 1. The division series are slated for Oct. 3-10 and the championship series Oct. 11-20. The World Series is set for Oct. 23-31.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="en" dir="ltr"><a href="https://x.com/hashtag/Postseason?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">#Postseason</a> baseball is right around the corner …<br><br>It all starts on September 29! <a href="https://t.co/2qKuhDQTv5">pic.twitter.com/2qKuhDQTv5</a></p>— MLB (@MLB) <a href="https://x.com/MLB/status/2086855575074132455?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">August 10, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p>The Cubs and Sox played in the wild-card round during the pandemic-shortened 2020 season, but no fans were in the stands. The Cubs lost to the Marlins in two games, and the Sox lost to the Athletics in three.</p><p>Neither team won their first-round series in 2008, either. The Cubs, who had the best record in the NL at 97-64, were swept by the Dodgers in the NLDS. The Sox needed a one-game playoff against the Twins to win the AL Central, but only after needing to beat the Tigers in a makeup game. They lost to the Rays in the ALDS in four games.</p><p>Both teams played on Oct. 2, the first time they played on the same day in the postseason since they played each other on Oct. 14, 1906, in Game 6 of the World Series, which the Sox won to take the crown.</p>

entries.title: Willie Wilson announces 4th run for Chicago mayor
entries.summary: <p>Chicago businessman Willie Wilson on Monday joined the race for mayor of Chicago — for the fourth time.</p><p>Wilson announced this candidacy Monday evening at a gathering of several dozen supporters in East Garfield Park. </p><p>"Everywhere I go, citizens ask me to represent the city of Chicago," Wilson said. "I believe in Chicago and I believe you deserve a leader who wakes up every morning ready to serve."</p><p>He joins a crowded field that already includes several public officeholders — but does not officially include the man occupying the mayor's office now.</p><p>In all, seven other people have announced the're running in next year's mayoral election. That includes two statewide officials, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2026/08/02/alexi-giannoulias-chicago-mayor-candidate-2027-february-election-secretary-of-state" >Secretary of State Alexi Giannoulias</a> and <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/city-hall/2026/06/03/state-comptroller-susana-mendoza-mayoral-campaign-brandon-johnson-alexi-giannoulias" >Comptroller Susana Mendoza</a>, as well as <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/fran-spielman-show/2026/01/07/us-rep-mike-quigley-mayoral-run-2027-brandon-johnson" >U.S. Rep. Mike Quigley</a> and Cook County Board of Review Commissioner George Cardenas.</p><p>Mayor Brandon Johnson has not officially declared <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/city-hall/2026/07/28/mayor-brandon-johnson-second-term-bid-no-decision-yet" >whether he will run for reelection</a>, though supporters have begun getting petitions signed on his behalf.</p><p>Without naming him, Wilson took a shot at Giannoulias for running for both mayor <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2026/07/15/alexi-giannoulias-brandon-johnson-potential-mayoral-candidates-campaign-fundraising-gap" target="_blank" >and secretary of state</a> simultaneously.</p><p>"Some politicians are running for this office at the same time they are standing for reelection for their current office in November. ... It may be legal, but it is morally wrong," Wilson said.</p><p>In 2019, Wilson fell short of the runoff, finishing fourth overall with 10.6% of the votes in the first round of balloting. Much of his support came from predominately Black wards on the South and West sides. He missed the runoff again in 2023 with a lower share of the vote — 9.13%.</p><p>In total, he has lost three nonpartisan mayoral elections, and ran unsuccessfully for president as a Democrat in 2016. In 2020, he unsuccessfully ran for U.S. Sen. Dick Durbin’s seat under the “Willie Wilson Party.”</p><p>Monday evening, Wilson said he is "not a politician. I'm a servant of God. I do not use big words. I speak plain and have good common sense.”</p><p>The perennial political candidate was among a small group of leaders in Chicago calling on President Donald Trump <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/politics/2025/08/27/willie-wilson-trump-national-guard" target="_blank" >to send the National Guard to Chicago</a>, citing the shooting death of his own son in 1995, and he applauded federal forces being deployed in Los Angeles to quell protests against immigration agents.</p><p>Last municipal election cycle, Wilson ran against COVID-19 safety measures — such as social distancing requirements for churches and vaccination mandates for city employees — while pushing to increase police salaries, and eliminating red-light and speed cameras. He again vowed to hire multiple police superintendents and said he would <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/city-hall/2022/7/13/23209738/willie-wilson-speech-violent-crime-chicago-police-2023-mayor-election-cta-red-light-cameras" >eliminate policies restricting police chases</a>.</p><p>Wilson has infused his campaign with $300,000 of his own money. He recently spent $27,000 on consulting and phone bills. In 2023, he donated $5 million to fund his campaign. In 2019, he gave his campaign $1.2 million.</p><p>Among his paid advisers is state Sen. Rickey Hendon. In 2023, Hendon was part of the Wilson campaign's push to <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/city-hall/2022/12/27/23528655/battle-on-sawyers-signatures-from-wilson-ally-continues" >challenge ballot petition signatures</a> collected by other candidates.</p><p>Ald. Ray Lopez (15th) was Wilson's sole City Council endorsement in the 2023 election. Lopez is putting his support behind Mendoza this time around, though he still considers Wilson a "close personal friend," Lopez told the Chicago Sun-Times on Monday. Lopez said Wilson would help make the race "dynamic" and "raise many of the issues that have been ignored" by Johnson's administration.</p><p>"Unfortunately some people are taking issue with this being his fourth attempt," Lopez said. "But I think it shows a commitment to this city, and the issues he's raised in prior campaigns haven't resolved themselves. Whatever his chances are, the man Willie Wilson continues to be a beacon of hope in this election that will be hard to ignore."</p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/politics/2025/08/27/willie-wilson-trump-national-guard" >Willie Wilson urges Trump to send National Guard to Chicago: ‘I welcome it’</a> </li> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/2022/4/11/23020331/willie-wilson-joins-2023-race-for-mayor-chicago-lightfoot-2019-endorsement-gasoline-giveaway" >Willie Wilson joins 2023 race for mayor</a> </li> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2023/2/1/23547878/willie-wilson-chicago-mayor-election-2023-business-property-tax-assistance-gas-food-giveaways" >Lightfoot challenger Willie Wilson calls 2019 endorsement of mayor ‘a helluva mistake’</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p></p>

entries.title: 2 adults dead in shooting inside Garfield Ridge elementary school, police say
entries.summary: <p>Two custodians were fatally shot inside Mark Twain Elementary School in Garfield Ridge on Monday afternoon in an apparent murder-suicide, according to preliminary police radio transmissions.</p><p>According to a statement from Chicago police, a 63-year-old man and 48-year-old woman were each found with a single gunshot wound to their heads inside the school in the 5100 block of South Lotus Avenue at 3:40 p.m. Both were taken to Christ Medical Center, where they were pronounced dead, police said. A weapon was recovered at the scene, police said.</p><p>According to police radio transmissions, a dispatcher said the shooting stemmed from a disagreement between two custodians. Both people were found inside Mark Twain Elementary School, according to the radio dispatches. One of them was found inside the school's lunchroom, the dispatcher said.</p><p>No students were at the school, as classes don't begin there until <a class="Link" href="https://app.smore.com/n/qew41" target="_blank" >August 24</a>. </p><p>Additional information was not immediately released.</p>

entries.title: Still chasing Brewers, Cubs driven to go deeper than last year’s playoff exit: ‘It’s on your mind every day’
entries.summary: <p>After their victory Friday against the Royals, the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs" target="_blank" >Cubs</a> were closer to the Brewers than they had been since the end of May, shrinking the gap between themselves and their National League Central-leading rivals to 4½ games.</p><p>Though only slightly, the margin is larger now.</p><p>Another year, another seemingly relentless grip on the NL Central by the team from north of the border.</p><p>For the last couple of months, the Cubs have been as good as they come, They have a 35-16 record since June 11 that’s tops in the NL and ranks second in the majors. Yet they’ve only made a small dent in the gap in the standings, with the Brewers entering Monday at 33-19 during the same span.</p><p>There’s a lot of baseball left before playoff seeds lock in, but should the Cubs start worrying about how — if — they’re going to catch the Brewers?</p><p>‘‘That’s not going to help,’’ manager Craig Counsell said last week. ‘‘We would like to make up ground, but worrying about it is not going to help me do it.</p><p>‘‘We’ve just got to do our thing.’’</p><p>The Cubs doing their thing has been darn effective, and they’re riding high after an eventful week that featured <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/08/03/cubs-mlb-trade-deadline-jed-hoyer-top-prospects-trades-kevin-gausman-clay-holmes-ryan-zeferjahn-braxton-garrett-tyrone-taylor" target="_blank" >trade-deadline reinforcements</a>, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/08/05/cubs-pete-crow-armstrong-shohei-ohtani-nl-mvp-race-dodgers-playoffs-craig-counsell-shota-imanaga" target="_blank" >a sweep of the Dodgers</a>, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/08/06/cubs-walk-off-win-alex-bregman-home-run-pete-crow-armstrong-stolen-base-blue-jays-dodgers-shohei-ohtani-nl-mvp" target="_blank" >a walk-off win against the Blue Jays</a> and a series triumph against the Royals that capped <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/08/08/cubs-pete-crow-armstrong-17-games-17-days-ian-happ-homer-clay-holmes-debut-injury-royals" target="_blank" >a stretch of 17 games in 17 days</a>.</p><p>But those Brewers just won’t stop.</p><p>The Cubs weren’t just bested in the division a year ago, but the Brewers bounced them from the postseason, too. With the Brewers owning four consecutive Central crowns — and five of the last six — what left-hander Matthew Boyd said in June is undoubtedly true: ‘‘The Central runs through them.’’</p><p>These Cubs excel at focusing on each new day, citing it as a key reason for their success. But <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/07/25/cubs-playoffs-brewers-pirates-nl-central-matthew-boyd-starting-rotation" target="_blank" >there’s a constant hunger</a>r that comes from that playoff exit. The goal from Day 1 has been to win the World Series.</p><p>‘‘It’s on your mind every day; that’s what you’re chasing,’’ right-hander Colin Rea said Sunday. ‘‘You’re in the present, trying to win this game today, but the end goal is to win the last game of the season.</p><p>‘‘That experience that guys got last year just fuels us even more. Guys saw how fun it was, how awesome Wrigley was at that time. You can’t match that feeling any other time during the season.</p><p>‘‘I can’t speak for everyone else, but I’m sure everyone’s just like, ‘Let’s get to that point.’ We’re in the dog days right now. Let’s get to that point of the season. That’s when the real fun begins.’’</p><p>Whether the Cubs catch the Brewers or not, they figure to be among the top contenders come October, waking up Monday with the fifth-best record in the majors.</p><p>Though team president Jed Hoyer frequently has cited the benefit of receiving a first-round bye into the NL Division Series, the Cubs certainly would be capable of making a lengthy run as a wild-card team.</p><p>In the final two months of the regular season, they’ll look to lock down one of those spots and ready themselves for the playoffs.</p><p>‘‘We can’t control what other teams are doing, if they’re winning or losing,’’ Rea said. ‘‘You’re in that in-between period of we still need to win games, but we also need to make sure we’re 100% — or as close to 100% as possible — going down the stretch, really communicating with guys and making sure guys are feeling good and we’re all on the same page.’’</p><p>After Hoyer’s work at the trade deadline, the Cubs seem well-positioned for a shot at October glory, with a deepened pitching staff to go along with a position-player group that has turned in impressive offensive numbers and <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/08/06/cubs-defense-mlb-trade-deadline-kevin-gausman-clay-holmes-gold-gloves-pitching-injuries-braxton-garrett" target="_blank" >dazzling defense</a>.</p><p>But this is August. They’ll need to be at their best two months from now to achieve their sky-high goals.</p><p>‘‘Our best baseball is still ahead of us,’’ Boyd said Sunday. ‘‘We’re playing great right now as a squad, collectively.</p><p>‘‘It’s a lot of fun to be in this clubhouse, a lot of fun to be a Cubbie. We’re excited for what’s ahead.’’</p><bsp-listcarousel class="PageListE" data-module data-column-count=3 data-hide-authors="true" data-hide-categories="true" data-hide-dates="true" entries.title: ICE amenaza con cargos penales al sheriff por no entregar a detenidos de la Cárcel del Condado de Cook
entries.summary: <p>Los funcionarios federales de control migratorio amenazaron con presentar cargos penales contra el Alguacil del Condado de Cook, Tom Dart, si no cumplía con las citaciones que solicitaban a su oficina la entrega de detenidos recluidos en la Cárcel del Condado de Cook.</p><p>Matt Walberg, portavoz de la oficina del alguacil, dijo que el Servicio de Inmigración y Control de Aduanas (ICE) envió las cuatro citaciones el mes pasado, junto con cartas que amenazaban a Dart.</p><p>The New York Times informó primero que ICE amenazó con acusar a Dart y a Dawanna S. Witt, la Alguacil del Condado de Hennepin, en Minnesota, que incluye Minneapolis.</p><div class="RichTextSidebarModule Enhancement" data-module data-align-center><a class="AnchorLink" id="module-0e0000" name="module-0e0000"></a> <div class="RichTextModule-items RichTextBody"><h3>La Voz Chicago WhatsApp</h3>Encuentra más noticias en nuestro canal de WhatsApp. <a class="Link" href="https://www.whatsapp.com/channel/0029Vb0XT1XCHDylm3rCs40P" target="_blank" ><b>Síguenos.</b></a></div> </div><p>Los condados que representan fueron sacudidos por campañas de deportación, que comenzaron en Chicago el año pasado.</p><p>Las tácticas de la administración cambiaron después de que agentes de control migratorio <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/immigration/2026/01/08/ice-shooting-minneapolis-chicago-homeland-security-immigration-deportation" target="_blank" >abatieron a tiros y mataron a dos ciudadanos estadounidenses</a> en Minneapolis, lo que provocó indignación y llamados a la reforma. Pero las cartas indican que las autoridades federales siguen centradas en Chicago y Minneapolis, las llamadas "ciudades santuario", con leyes destinadas a impedir que los agentes locales de la ley cooperen con la ejecución de la ley migratoria civil.</p><p>Dart recibió citaciones por separado exigiendo que su oficina permitiera que cuatro detenidos acudieran a entrevistas en las oficinas de ICE en el Loop o que los entregaran al ser puestos en libertad. Sin embargo, tres ya habían sido liberados de la cárcel, dijo Walberg.</p><p>Una carta adjunta decía que el incumplimiento de la citación "puede constituir obstrucción a un testigo y, si hay condena, puede resultar en multas y en una pena de prisión".</p><p>Walberg destacó que la oficina del alguacil está obligada a mantener a los detenidos bajo custodia y no puede liberarlos para entrevistas con otras agencias de aplicación de la ley ni entregarlos cuando son puestos en libertad.</p><p>La alguacil Witt emitió un comunicado en el que dijo que las amenazas de enjuiciamiento que recibió "no me harán abandonar mis responsabilidades legales ni desatender las protecciones constitucionales. Mi prioridad sigue siendo desempeñar mi trabajo conforme a la ley y no responder a la presión política ni a la intimidación".</p><p>La portavoz de Witt, Rebecca Aurelious, comentó que la oficina también recibió citaciones para detenidos que ya habían sido liberados.</p><p>Un portavoz del Departamento de Seguridad Nacional (DHS) dijo que es práctica habitual citar a funcionarios locales del orden que "se negaron a cooperar con las autoridades federales de inmigración y con ‘las órdenes de detención’”. El portavoz agregó que la táctica también se usó durante el primer mandato de Trump.</p><p>"Seguimos con estos esfuerzos mientras los políticos de las 'ciudades santuario' se niegan a entregar a los peores delincuentes extranjeros indocumentados", dijo el portavoz. "Las jurisdicciones no cooperativas tienen una elección: dejar de acoger a delincuentes extranjeros indocumentados y liberarlos en sus comunidades, o trabajar con ICE para que Estados Unidos vuelva a ser seguro”.</p><p>“De cualquier manera, ICE no frenará la aplicación de la ley federal”, enfatizó.</p><p><i>Traducido con una herramienta de inteligencia artificial (IA) y editado por los seres humanos de </i><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/la-voz" target="_blank" ><i>La Voz Chicago</i></a><br></p>

entries.title: Englewood homes sold under city program aimed to rehab abandoned properties
entries.summary: <p>Chicago’s effort to rehabilitate abandoned homes on the South and West sides to foster homeownership took a big step recently.</p><p>The city, along with project partners and neighbors, held a ribbon-cutting Friday on two rehabbed homes on South Green Street in Englewood. One already has been sold and the other is under contract.</p><p>The homes join more than 70 other properties rehabbed and sold under <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/real-estate/2026/05/22/city-program-rebuild-chicago-rehab-30-properties-south-west-sides" >Rebuild Chicago 2.0</a>, an expansion of the city’s Rebuild program that gives abandoned homes a second life. The program identifies homes that can be acquired, rehabbed and sold to create homeownership opportunities on the South and West sides, which have experienced decades of disinvestment.</p><div entries.title: CPD officer who shot Derek Jordan 'ignored every opportunity to de-escalate,' family alleges in lawsuit
entries.summary: <p>A Chicago police officer was in a "reckless and uncontrolled state of mind" when he fatally shot Derek Jordan earlier this year in Humboldt Park, his family alleges in a lawsuit.</p><p>According to police, Jordan, 42, was fleeing officers around 5:30 p.m. on March 9 when they caught up to him in an alley in the 800 block of North Homan Avenue. Jordan was boxed in by Chicago Police Department squad cars, a CTA bus and a parked car. </p><p>Officers repeatedly yelled for Jordan to get out of his car, but he kept trying to drive off and crashed into the bus and a police vehicle, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/police-reform/2026/05/11/chicago-police-shooting-cpd-derek-jordan-humboldt-park-body-cam" target="_blank" >video footage from the scene shows</a>. </p><p>Within seconds of arriving, one officer pulled out his gun and screamed at Jordan: “Get out of the f - - - - - - car or I’ll kill you. I’ll kill you."</p><p>About 20 seconds later, he fired six shots into Jordan's car. </p><p>The Romanucci and Blandin law firm is representing Jordan's family, and it filed the lawsuit Friday. The firm held a news conference Monday afternoon laying out the allegations in its lawsuit, which names the city of Chicago and the police officer who shot Jordan as defendants.</p><p>The officer "came in unjustifiably hot to a scene in which Derek was inside a car that was blocked by several police officers," said Antonio Romanucci, one of the lawyers representing Jordan's family.</p><p>Those officers already on the scene were "working to de-escalate the situation," Romanucci added. But the officer who shot Jordan "ignored any opportunity to calm the scene, to de-escalate and do what police officers are supposed to do."</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div The Civilian Office of Police Accountability is investigating the incident. A COPA spokesperson said Monday that investigation remains ongoing. </p><p>Romanucci also called on Cook County State's Attorney Eileen O'Neill Burke to investigate the incident and consider murder charges against the officer. A spokesperson for Burke said the state's attorney's office will review the incident after the police department and COPA have completed their own investigations. </p><p>Christine and Derek Thompkins, Jordan's parents, attended Monday's news conference. They said Jordan's death has left them devastated.</p><p>“I have a hole in my heart," Derek Thompkins said. "I miss my son, and his dying this way has ruined every day for me. entries.title: Bears' offense hasn't been this stacked in more than a decade, and it's built to withstand injuries
entries.summary: <p>From the moment <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a> coach Ben Johnson got to Halas Hall and began writing up a shopping list for general manager Ryan Poles and the personnel department, his plan was to fortify the roster with so many offensive weapons that nothing could stop them.</p><p>For every move an opposing defense could make, he’d have a countermove. There’d be seemingly no end to the wrinkles of his scheme and the chess pieces at his disposal.</p><p>And finally, the Bears are there.</p><p>Even after unloading wide receiver DJ Moore to save salary-cap space and even with some high-potential, unproven talent, this is the most dangerous array of threats the Bears have put together in over a decade. In some cases it might be overkill, though Johnson surely would disagree.</p><p>The last time they were this loaded, arguably, was in 2013 with Jay Cutler at quarterback. Running back Matt Forte was still in his prime as an excellent runner and receiver. Wide receivers Alshon Jeffery and Brandon Marshall each topped 1,200 yards, and Martellus Bennett was a top-10 tight end.</p><p>Those Bears were a disaster defensively and finished 8-8 under Marc Trestman, but they sure were fun to watch when they had the ball. They still stand as the second-highest scoring Bears team in the Super Bowl era at 27.8 points per game.</p><p>Johnson would like to blow all the Bears’ records out of the water this season, and that will hinge primarily on quarterback <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2025/08/31/why-do-so-many-people-hate-bears-qb-caleb-williams-he-answers-exactly-that-question" >Caleb Williams</a>’ ability to sharpen the finer points of his position to become a passer who can play both efficiently and spectacularly. There certainly is an abundance of options, though, when he drops back to throw.</p><p>The Bears have former 2024 No. 9 overall pick Rome Odunze as their go-to wide receiver, but Johnson has high expectations for second-year Luther Burden as well. He also brought in an ideal No. 3 at the position by reconnecting with 10-year veteran Kalif Raymond, whom he coached for four seasons with the Lions.</p><p>Johnson stacked the tight end room with Colston Loveland (a popular pick to be an All-Pro this season), Cole Kmet and third-round pick Sam Roush, and the Bears have reliable running backs in D’Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai.</p><p>Not only does all of that open new chapters of the playbook for Johnson, but it shields the Bears against injuries on that side of the ball. No one player going down would sink the whole thing.</p><p>The first hit to that group came Saturday when Burden left practice with a groin injury, and Johnson told the Sun-Times on Monday that he’ll be <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/08/10/bears-luther-burden-groin-injury-preseason-miss-nfl-wide-receiver-practice-tyrique-stevenson" >out the rest of the preseason,</a> but is expected to be ready for the Sept. 13 season opener at the Panthers.</p><p>That’s certainly a downer, but hardly devastating, even if he ends up missing a regular-season game or two.</p><p>The roster has been developed to a point where that’s true of basically any wide receiver, tight end or running back. The Bears went without Odunze for a while last season and were fine. When Swift was out, Monangai shined. Loveland is the focal point at tight end, but Kmet has a lot of big games on his résumé.</p><p>At the end of the Ryan Pace and Matt Nagy run in 2021, the Bears had little outside of Kmet and wide receiver Darnell Mooney, and running back David Montgomery was good, but not much of a homerun threat. It didn’t get much better until 2024 when Swift came aboard and the Bears drafted Odunze and traded for Keenan Allen to join Moore at receiver.</p><p>That talent, however, was in shaky hands with coach Matt Eberflus and offensive coordinator Shane Waldron, and Williams was hardly ready to run a thriving offense.</p><p>It started to turn last year when Johnson pushed for the Bears to draft Loveland (No. 10 overall) and Burden (No. 39) and developed Monangai (a seventh-rounder) into one of the best runners of his draft class. Those were long-term investments, though they paid off early as Loveland led the team in yards receiving and Monangai rushed for 783 yards and five touchdowns.</p><p>Burden is the key to putting the offense over the top this season, and it’ll be a challenge for him to stay dialed in while hurt. He played just 35% of the snaps last season as he acclimated to Johnson’s offense and the league at large.</p><p>His role is going to depend on how well he knows the playbook, and that seems to be going well. It’s difficult to imagine Johnson touting him as the next big thing all offseason if he wasn’t sure about that part of it.</p><p>“I’m way more confident,” Burden said last week. “I’m able to play faster than I was. I feel good about the playbook — where I need to be and how I need to get there.”</p><p>With such a diversified offense, it likely will be difficult for any one player to hit statistical milestones this season, but it’s hard to get caught up in that if the Bears are scoring and winning. It gives Johnson a chance to showcase the full extent of his creativity.</p><p></p><bsp-list-loadmore class="PageListH" data-module data-hide-authors="true" data-hide-categories="true" entries.title: 56 boxes of ashes taken from funeral home where decomposing bodies were found
entries.summary: <p>Besides the 56 bodies found at the South Chicago Chapel last week, authorities also found 56 boxes of cremated remains, officials confirmed Monday. </p><p>A spokesperson for the Cook County medical examiner’s office said it is storing the cremated remains that were found at the funeral home, and that the Chicago Police Department is locating next of kin for these remains. </p><p>The cremated remains were brought to the medical examiner's office about 1 a.m. Saturday after the execution of a search warrant at South Chicago Chapel, according to police. Officers were asked to escort the 56 boxes of ashes which police also discovered in the chapel to the medical examiner’s office, according to a report from the city’s Office of Emergency Management and Communications.</p><p>Also Monday, the medical examiner’s office announced it has positively identified 11 of the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/news/2026/08/06/decomposing-bodies-found-funeral-home-south-chicago-chapel-95th-street" >56 bodies found in the funeral home</a>, and that 10 of those families have been notified. So far, two bodies have been released to funeral homes. The office continues to work with local and state authorities to identify the remaining 45 bodies.</p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/morning-edition/2026/08/10/south-chicago-chapel-chicago-public-schools-lake-shore-drive" >Families shocked by decomposing bodies at funeral home</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p></p>
